headline: South Asia: Saudi Arabia accuses Iran of encouraging Houthis in latest escalation
script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Saudi Arabia accuses Iran of encouraging Houthis in latest escalation.
- India: Yemen claims over 700 Houthis killed after 1,250 strikes rained within 24 hours.
- Asia: ‘We’re done’: Ukraine resumes Russian refinery strikes, defying Trump.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
The Caribbean - bottom line: Reckoning over rights - Osborne challenges Chang’s stance on US deportation lawsuits, warns Jamaica could face scrutiny over rights safeguards.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 15 hours ago: Reckoning over rights - Osborne challenges Chang’s stance on US deportation lawsuits, warns Jamaica could face scrutiny over rights safeguards.
National Security Minister Dr Horace Chang’s assertion that legal challenges in the United States (US) against its third-country deportation policy are of no concern to Jamaica has drawn criticism from civil society advocate Kay Osborne. Osborne described Chang’s statement as a “convenient deflection”, arguing that it sidesteps the Government’s responsibility to protect human rights under international law, including the obligation not to transfer people to places where they face torture or persecution.
United States - bottom line: US Army eyes developing soldier-worn drone detection gear.
- Military Times, just now: US Army eyes developing soldier-worn drone detection gear.
The Army is in the early stages of developing and testing a wearable or lightweight device that could alert soldiers to the presence of hostile drones.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

Two Russian drones have hit a warehouse in Kyiv's Sviatoshynskyi district, sparking a fire. Earlier, a drone crash in the Pecherskyi district injured seven people.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 2 hours ago: CNN reports Ukraine has run out of Patriot missiles.
Ukraine has run out of interceptor missiles for its US-made Patriot air defence systems, leaving the country more vulnerable to Russian ballistic attacks.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 3 hours ago: Putin threatens Ukraine with retaliation over strikes on Russian oil refineries: "They started this".
Ignoring the so-called "energy ceasefire" announced by Donald Trump, Russian leader Vladimir Putin has threatened retaliation against Ukraine for alleged strikes on oil refineries.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Black Sea Drone Attacks Expose Holes in Bulgarian Security Strategy.
- Balkan Insight, 14 hours ago: Black Sea Drone Attacks Expose Holes in Bulgarian Security Strategy.

Edi Rama accuses opposition of trying to 'pull Albania down' after a second night of violence saw government buildings and businesses attacked and set on fire amid clashes between student protesters and police.
- Politico Europe, one hour ago: ‘No logic’: Finland slams Trump for siding with Putin against Ukraine.
Prime Minister Petteri Orpo tells POLITICO the U.S. is going against its allies and warns Europe must find a way to keep Ukraine in the fight, even if it means reopening the debate over raiding Russian assets.
- Politico Europe, 2 hours ago: Macron warns EU leaders they need to agree budget by end of year.
Starting from January, there will be no political room for concluding an agreement, French president tells summit.

Though an expert from the Royal United Services Institute said that the Houthis needed to be defeated, he insisted this could only come about by empowering the legitimate government - not airstrikes.

- Africanews, 7 hours ago: Pakistan: Classrooms reduced to rubble in deadly school disaster, at leat 32 pupils killed.
A school roof collapsed in Peshawar, northwestern Pakistan, on Thursday 15 October, killing at least 32 pupils and a teacher. Officials said the roof was structurally weak and had been overloaded by construction work. The school’s owner was arrested and an investigation launched.

[New Zimbabwe] THE Zambezi River Authority (ZRA) has slashed water allocations for power generation at Kariba Dam to 23 billion cubic metres (BCM) in 2027, warning of a potentially dry season due to El Niño conditions.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Saudi Arabia accuses Iran of encouraging Houthis in latest escalation.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 6 hours ago: Saudi Arabia accuses Iran of encouraging Houthis in latest escalation.
A Saudi foreign ministry official on Thursday accused Iran of encouraging the Houthis in the latest escalation of their fight with the kingdom, adding that it continues to arm and train the group. “Iran continues to arm, train and support the Houthi militia in violation of UN security council resolutions,” Dr Rayed Krimly, deputy minister for public diplomacy at the foreign ministry, said during a virtual briefing with reporters. “We think that the escalation by the Houthis at this latest stage of the conflict is encouraged by Iran,” he later said.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 12 hours ago: Elon Musk calls on Zelensky to 'go' as Ukraine leader.
Tech billionaire Elon Musk called on Wednesday for Volodymyr Zelensky to “go” as Ukraine’s president, as Kyiv raised doubts over US support for the war-torn country. Ukraine accused the United States this week of helping Russia by failing to warn it of incoming missile strikes and hobbling Kyiv’s military response through changes to Musk’s satellite system which it uses for communications. “And so the slaughter continues,” Musk wrote on X.
- Dawn (Pakistan), one hour ago: At UNSC, Pakistan condemns Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, reaffirms support for kingdom's security.
WASHINGTON: Pakistan on Thursday strongly condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia’s civilian and economic infrastructure, reaffirming its support for the kingdom’s security and right to self-defence amid escalating regional tensions. Speaking at a United Nations Security Council (UNSC) debate on the Middle East, Pakistan’s acting Permanent Representative, Ambassador Usman Jadoon, said, “These attacks must cease immediately.” He reiterated Islamabad’s support for efforts to secure a peaceful settlement in Yemen.
- Dawn (Pakistan), NDTV - Top Stories, one hour ago: US considers hitting Iran with 'Mother of All Bombs': report.
The United States is considering using its biggest non-nuclear bomb against Iran if President Donald Trump should decide to renew combat in the war that has hit a deadlock, CNN reported on Thursday. The military is planning for the potential use of the GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast (MOAB) bomb — better known by its nickname, the “Mother Of All Bombs” — to target Iranian energy infrastructure and nuclear sites, according to the news outlet, which quoted officials familiar with the matter.
India - bottom line: Yemen claims over 700 Houthis killed after 1,250 strikes rained within 24 hours.
- Times of India - Top Stories, South China Morning Post - China, NDTV - Top Stories, The Hindu - International, Al Jazeera - Middle East, 2 hours ago: Yemen claims over 700 Houthis killed after 1,250 strikes rained within 24 hours.
Yemen armed forces reported conducting 1,250 targeting operations against Houthis in one day. These strikes coincided with Houthi attacks on Aden’s presidential palace, resulting in casualties. Houthi spokesperson denied claims of missile strikes towards Medina, asserting their innocence. Meanwhile, the Saudi-led coalition intercepted several missiles aimed at its territories amid ongoing tensions. Overall, hostilities between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia have intensified over recent months.
- NDTV - Top Stories, Africanews, one hour ago: Saudi-Led Coalition Says Houthis Attacked Riyadh Airport 20 Times This Month.
The Houthis have been firing ballistic missiles and drones at key Saudi sites for a week, in response to the kingdom's backing of government forces in Yemen's renewed civil war. The coalition's latest statement highlighted the risk to Saudi civilian infrastructure as the conflict escalated.
- NDTV - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: "Stay Indoors In Case Of Aerial Attack": Fresh Advisory For Indians In Saudi.
The updated advisory comes amid escalating tensions in the region due to a series of drone and missile attacks targeting civilian infrastructure by Yemen's Houthis.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 4 hours ago: Andhra Pradesh shocker: Lover lured to pond, beaten to death; husband, wife arrested.
Mamidi Gouri Shankar and his wife, Mamidi Lakshmi Durga, are accused of orchestrating Thumula Lakshmana's murder. Lakshmana allegedly had an extramarital affair with Lakshmi Durga, leading to disputes with her husband. Following a planned attack, he was murdered and his body dumped in a canal. Police arrested several individuals linked to the crime, including the couple, as the investigation progressed.

Nepal has weathered three disasters in six weeks, including the deadly August flash flood, making this year one of the deadliest in a country where monsoon rains already frequently wreak havoc. Experts warn that climate change is only making matters worse. Authorities in the central Chinese province of Hunan have warned of the potential risks of cross-border arranged marriages, saying some relationships lack genuine emotional foundations and can lead to financial ruin or legal trouble. Marriages can be risky when they are organised by illegal matchmaking agencies that charge high fees, according to a post on the Xintian county police branch’s social media account on Tuesday. For-profit international matchmaking is illegal in China. The post...

A grassland fire in Mongolia has raised fresh concerns in China, underscoring the recurring risk of cross-border environmental hazards. This is not the first time an environmental disaster originating in Mongolia has threatened to cross the 4,700km (2,920-mile) border into China, with the impacts sometimes also affecting the Korean peninsula and Japan.
